questions.question: According to the experiments, what is one major advantage of Generation‑Augmented Retrieval (GAR) when combined with BM25?

options.A: It reduces the size of the index.
options.B: It achieves significant gains over BM25 with original queries.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any query expansion.
options.D: It requires less computational time than BM25 alone.

questions.explanation:
The text states that GAR combined with BM25 achieves significant gains over the same BM25 model that uses the original queries or existing unsupervised query expansion methods. (Source Page: [2])  

---

questions.question: On which two benchmark datasets were the extensive experiments for GAR conducted?
questions.explanation:
The context explicitly mentions experiments on the Natural Questions (NQ) and TriviaQA datasets. (Source Page: [2])  

---

questions.question: Which neural retrieval model is evaluated alongside GAR in the top‑k retrieval accuracy comparison?
questions.explanation:
Table 4 compares BM25, BM25 + RM3, DPR, GAR, and GAR + DPR, indicating that DPR is the neural model evaluated with GAR. (Source Page: [6])

questions.question: What is the ROUGE‑1 F1 score for the generation‑augmented query when using the “answer” style on the NQ dataset?
questions.explanation:
The ROUGE‑1/2/L F1 scores for the generation‑augmented query (answer) on NQ are reported as 7.05/2.84/5.62. (Source Page: [6])

questions.question: Which unsupervised query expansion method is specifically mentioned as a baseline in the retrieval experiments?
questions.explanation:
The comparison includes “BM25 with query expansion (+RM3)”, identifying RM3 as the unsupervised QE baseline. (Source Page: [6])
